thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — Canary failure detected for rollout 'stable-2026-03-15'. error_rate(5m) = 6.8% (>5% threshold) on service inference-eu-west1. Affected route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-7b-q4). Pods showing restarts and elevated 5xx. Paging eng-oncall.

deploy-bot: Deployment stable-2026-03-15 started at 2056789005 by @elaine. Canary traffic = 3% (eu-west). Config changes: feature-flag kvcache-v2 = ON; kernel patch qkernel-v2 applied to canary nodes.

ryan: ack, i'm oncall — grabbing dashboards and logs now. Which canary subset is impacted?

maria: i'm oncall. Confirming errors: 5xx spike aligns with canary cohort in eu-west. Tail latency > 2s for /v1/generate for ~7% of canary requests. No deploy job failures yet, but pod restarts + OOMs shown in kube events.

elaine: I rolled kvcache-v2 to ON for the canary to test hot-prefix caching. Rolling it back now for canary. If that doesn't fix it, i'll rollback the canary revision.

elaine: Executing toggle now — using internal feature flag service: 
```
curl -X PATCH 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_API' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  https://ff.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/kvcache-v2/scope/canary 
  -d '{"state": "off"}'
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag change accepted. kvcache-v2 scope=canary set to OFF.

maria: seeing partial improvement within 30s — error rate down to 3.2%, tail latency still elevated on a small subset. Looks like there are stale kernels on some nodes. Will try a controlled drain of one failing pod to force scheduling on non-qkernel nodes.

oncall-l2: stepping in to assist with rollback if needed. If drain + flag toggle doesn't resolve in 5m, plan: abort canary and rollback to stable revision stable-2026-03-14.

ryan: can you run the drain command and capture the pod logs?

maria: running drain and collecting logs. Logs show repeated errors: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] quant-kernel: failed to init resource: incompatible driver version
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] inference: kernel fallback triggered, slower path; subsequent memory thrash and OOM killer invoked
```

maria: drain completed for pod inference-eu-west1-pod-27; new pod scheduled on node with qkernel-v1. Error rate improving to 0.9% after reschedule.

elaine: thanks. i'm going to roll the canary back entirely to previous image and clear canary routing quickly: 
```
# abort canary and route 0% to new revision
redwoodctl rollout abort --service inference --revision stable-2026-03-15 --scope canary
redwoodctl rollout promote --service inference --revision stable-2026-03-14 --scope canary
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job started by @elaine at 2056789038.

maria: metrics now: error_rate(5m) = 0.4% (below threshold), p95 latency back to normal. No customer-wide outage, but clients routed through eu-west canary saw increased 5xxs between 14:00-14:05 UTC.

ryan: customers impacted estimated ~1.2% of global traffic — noted client reports from internal search-saas and external customer acme-marketing experiencing timeouts. Opening incident ticket INC-12345 and notifying support to reach out to affected customers.

oncall-l2: Handing off to L2 for deeper postmortem and kernel/hardware correlation. @manny will own the follow-up to validate driver compatibility matrix and gate future rollouts.

manny: i'll take it. initial hypothesis: qkernel-v2 introduces a driver mismatch on older EC2 instances; need to add node selector or add canary gating step.

ryan: summary for handoff — mitigation done: kvcache-v2 turned off for canary, canary aborted and rolled back to stable-2026-03-14, pod drains scheduled. Current state: service healthy, error rate back under SLO. Next steps: postmortem with timeline, assign kernel compatibility task, add additional canary observability (kernel-level health, driver mismatches) and pre-rollout gating. Severity S2.

elaine: i'll collate change set and push to postmortem draft. Thanks for quick responses everyone. :thumbsup:

ryan: closing paging loop. If anyone sees residual anomalies, ping this thread.
